name: Xiaoyao-san (Xiaoyao formula)
short: Review: liver injury case reports and series with Jia Wei Xia Yao San, Kamishoyosan (link not stated). Trial reviews: fewer adverse events than Western medicine, or none serious; one: safety unclear.
text: A review of herbal hepatotoxicity from traditional Chinese medicine reported that case reports and case series published since 2011 provided evidence of liver injury from several products, among them Jia Wei Xia Yao San (as spelled in the abstract) and Kamishoyosan; the abstract does not say how these products relate to Xiaoyao-san or what they contain, and does not give the number or severity of the cases. In trials, a meta-analysis of six randomised trials (707 participants) in functional dyspepsia found adverse events less frequent with Xiaoyao-san, alone or combined, than with conventional medicine alone, and a meta-analysis of seven trials (607 patients) of the formula added to antidepressants for post-stroke depression observed no serious adverse events. In a placebo-controlled trial of Jiawei Xiaoyao pill (the abstract does not describe its contents or its relation to Xiaoyao-san) in 144 women with premenstrual syndrome, adverse events, severe adverse events and withdrawals did not differ significantly between groups. A review of Xiaoyao-san preparations for Hashimoto's thyroiditis concluded that their safety profile remains unclear. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
